headline: This law creates a faster, cheaper bankruptcy reorganization path for small businesses under Chapter 11 and changes some related court rules.
what_it_does: The law sets up new Chapter 11 procedures for small businesses. A court-appointed trustee helps the business build a repayment plan, tracks its property, and makes sure it makes required payments. Only the business owner or debtor can file a reorganization plan under these procedures, and a court can approve a plan over creditor objections if it is fair and equitable and does not discriminate unfairly. The law also raises the dollar threshold for certain debt-collection lawsuits against noninsiders from $13,650 to $25,000, and it limits when a trustee can cancel certain pre-bankruptcy payments.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization
who_it_affects.how: They can use new procedures with a trustee, reduced disclosure requirements, and a plan that the court may approve even if creditors object.

who_it_affects.group: Creditors of small businesses in Chapter 11
who_it_affects.how: They can no longer submit their own reorganization plans under these procedures and may have a plan approved over their objection if it meets the law's fairness standards.

who_it_affects.group: Debtors who must pay under a reorganization plan
who_it_affects.how: They must commit projected disposable income for three to five years toward plan payments and submit future income to the trustee as needed.

who_it_affects.group: Creditors who received payments from a debtor before bankruptcy
who_it_affects.how: A trustee must use reasonable due diligence and consider known defenses before voiding those payments as preferential transfers.

who_it_affects.group: Parties sued to recover small debts connected to a Chapter 11 case
who_it_affects.how: Lawsuits to recover debts under $25,000 from noninsiders must be filed in the court where the defendant lives, up from the previous $13,650 limit.

when_it_takes_effect: 180 days after enactment, which was August 23, 2019.
